# Autoshop — M1 Implementation Plan

> **Historical planning document (2026-06).** It records the decisions and the
> evidence available *when M1 was planned*; several of them were later reversed
> by shipped code (the decode stack is `rawler` alone, config is JSON in the
> per-user store rather than TOML beside the checkout, the XMP projection lives
> in that store rather than beside the RAW, and the Kelvin/era rules changed in
> v0.14–v0.16 and again in v0.19.0, which recalibrated `kelvin_to_rgb`'s
> cool-side coefficients away from the published Tanner-Helland constants so the
> branches meet at 6600 K — see V2_PLAN §4a). Present-tense statements below describe the plan, not today's
> behaviour — for that read [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md), [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md)
> and the code. Corrections are inlined only where a stale claim would mislead
> someone changing that subsystem today.

> Synthesis of five research reports against the live scaffold ([src/recipe.rs](../src/recipe.rs), [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](../docs/ARCHITECTURE.md), [Cargo.toml](../Cargo.toml)). Evidence tags are preserved from the source reports; `[verified: …]` = read from a primary source this research session, `[unverified]` = not yet confirmed against a real file/API. The authoritative `EditRecipe` field set is the one in `src/recipe.rs` (Report 2's schema was illustrative; Report 5 read the real one).

M1 scope (from [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:83-84](../docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)): RAW decode + features, unified provider framework, GPT image advisor, Claude verifier. XMP sidecar writer is M2 in the doc, but Reports 4 & 5 fully spec it and it is the primary deliverable — this plan includes a **decode-time spec lock** for it in M1 and the writer build in M2.

## 1. Decode stack decision: `rawloader` + `imagepipe` (primary), `rawler` (fallback)

**Decision: ship M1 on `rawloader` 0.37.1 + `imagepipe` 0.5.0, but design the decode module behind a `Decoder` trait so `rawler` 0.7.2 can be swapped in for any of the three gaps below.**

Rationale:
- `rawloader` **does decode Sony ARW** (dedicated `src/decoders/arw.rs`) and is pure-Rust → no C toolchain on Windows [verified: https://github.com/pedrocr/rawloader/tree/master/src/decoders]. It returns sensor mosaic + the calibration metadata we need (make/model, WB coeffs, black/white levels, CFA, color matrix, crops, orientation) [verified: docs.rs RawImage struct]. *v0.30.0 correction: the shipped decoder is `rawler` 0.7.2, whose `RawImage.orientation` is HARD-CODED to `Normal` for every decoder except DNG/QTK (upstream `// TODO fixme`) — never read that field; the real EXIF tag 0x0112 comes via `decode::raw_orientation_of` on `RawMetadata.exif`.* *v0.32.0 correction, the same shape one level down: “crops” does not arrive either. For an ARW rawler builds `active_area` from the `SonyRawImageSize` tag, which carries a SIZE, so its origin is pinned at `(0, 0)` (`decoders/arw.rs:707`), and its `CropDefault` step applies the DNG default crop only `if crop.d != intermediate.dim()` (`imgop/develop.rs:216`) — which a pure TRANSLATION never satisfies. Net: every Sony ARW developed from the sensor's top-left corner instead of from `DefaultCropOrigin = (32, 20)`, measured as a `(+31 ± 6, +20 ± 1)` px offset against Lightroom's own export on eight frames. `decode::align_default_crop` moves the demosaic ROI onto the declared rectangle before the develop; `decode::frame_size` is the read-only accessor for the same rectangle.*
- `imagepipe` is the companion that turns the mosaic into demosaiced sRGB for the histogram/clipping render [verified: imagepipe depends on rawloader; `SRGBImage` = "RawImage processed into a full 8bit sRGB image with levels and gamma"].
- libraw is rejected: `libraw-rs` is **0.0.4, last published 2021-02-02**, pre-alpha, requires building/linking the C lib [verified: https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/libraw-rs]. Not worth the Windows FFI cost when a maintained pure-Rust fallback exists.

**Three known gaps in the `rawloader`+`imagepipe` stack — and the fallback that closes them:**
1. **No embedded JPEG-preview/thumbnail extraction at all** — `rawloader` exposes no preview field/method [verified: struct page lists none]. The advisor needs a preview image, so this gap is load-bearing.
2. **No full EXIF** (ISO/shutter/aperture/lens/as-shot WB) — only camera-calibration metadata [verified: struct fields].
3. **Stale camera DB** — frozen April 2022; **no A7 IV / A7R IV/V / A1 / A9 II / A6700 / A7C II** etc. (newest body is A7 III / A9, 2017–2018) [verified: directory listing has none of these].

`rawler` 0.7.2 (dnglab, published 2026-02-26) closes all three: ARW supported, `raw_metadata()` (full EXIF), `preview_image()` / `thumbnail_image()` (embedded preview), and a current camera DB [verified: https://github.com/dnglab/dnglab + docs.rs Decoder trait]. Caveat: its API is explicitly **not SemVer-stable** per dnglab README [verified] — pin the exact version.

**Practical M1 path for the preview + EXIF problem:** since `rawloader` gives neither, M1 should use **`rawler` for preview-JPEG extraction + EXIF**, and `rawloader`+`imagepipe` (or `rawler`'s `raw_image`) for the sensor/histogram render. Net: depend on `rawler` from day one for the advisor-feeding path; keep `imagepipe` only if a pure-Rust sRGB pipeline is preferred for the histogram. This is a single decisive recommendation from Report 1's own conclusion ("Use `rawler` as the primary decoder if you need ARW preview-JPEG extraction, full EXIF, or post-2018 bodies").

**Decision refinement:** Primary = **`rawler` 0.7.2** for preview + EXIF + raw image (covers all bodies, all three gaps). Keep `rawloader`+`imagepipe` available behind the same trait as the LGPL pure-Rust option for pre-2019 bodies if a `rawler` build issue arises on Windows. Pin both.

[unverified] `RawSource::new` exact constructor signature and the `image` crate re-export path in rawler 0.7.2 — API is unstable; run `cargo doc` on the pinned release before relying on exact call shapes.
[unverified] whether `libraw-rs` 0.0.4 builds against current LibRaw on Windows (not tested — and we are not using it).

## 2. Unified `Advisor` trait — final Rust signature + module layout

The trait must match the architecture's two roles ([docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:54-72](../docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)): **GPT vision → `propose`**, **Claude data-only → `verify`**. I align the method names with the ARCHITECTURE.md sketch (`propose`/`verify`) rather than Report 3's `image_to_recipe`/`verify` names, because the doc is the project contract. *(Correction, v0.26.2: the shipped framework later grew a third, trait-external role — the R20 visual judge, `advisor::judge` — see ARCHITECTURE §3; the two-role trait itself is unchanged.)*

**Async on tokio, `#[async_trait]` for `dyn` object-safety** [verified: reqwest async runs on tokio; async fn in traits is stable since Rust 1.75 but **not dyn-compatible** — `async_trait` desugars to `Pin<Box<dyn Future>>` to restore object safety, https://blog.rust-lang.org/2023/12/28/Rust-1.75.0/ + https://docs.rs/async-trait/]. Claude side shells out via `tokio::process::Command` [verified: docs.rs tokio process].

```rust
// src/advisor/mod.rs
use async_trait::async_trait;

/// Preview image fed to the vision advisor (embedded JPEG from the RAW).
pub struct Preview { pub bytes: Vec<u8>, pub mime: String }   // e.g. "image/jpeg"

/// Decode-time features both roles reason over (EXIF + histogram/clipping stats).
pub struct Meta {
    pub make: String,
    pub model: String,
    pub iso: Option<u32>,
    pub shutter: Option<String>,
    pub aperture: Option<f32>,
    pub lens: Option<String>,
    pub as_shot_wb_k: Option<f32>,
    pub histogram: Histogram,        // clipping %, per-channel bins
}

/// Verifier outcome — see §4 for the full type.
pub struct Verdict {
    pub decision: Decision,          // Accept | Revise | Reject
    pub reasons: Vec<String>,
    pub revised_hint: Option<String>,
}
pub enum Decision { Accept, Revise, Reject }

#[async_trait]
pub trait Advisor: Send + Sync {
    fn name(&self) -> &'static str;

    /// Image role (GPT vision): preview + metadata -> EditRecipe.
    async fn propose(&self, img: &Preview, meta: &Meta)
        -> Result<crate::recipe::EditRecipe, AdvisorError>;

    /// Analyst role (Claude, data-only): acceptance-verify the recipe.
    async fn verify(&self, recipe: &crate::recipe::EditRecipe, meta: &Meta)
        -> Result<Verdict, AdvisorError>;
}
```

- `Send + Sync` supertrait so `Box<dyn Advisor>` crosses tokio worker threads [verified: tokio multi-thread runtime requires Send to move across workers].
- A provider may not support a method (Claude does no vision in M1): return `Err` rather than panic. Single-trait keeps the provider registry uniform [verified-design, Report 3 B4].

**Error type** (`thiserror` in the lib, `anyhow` only at `main`) [verified: docs.rs thiserror `#[from]`; anyhow for application top-level]:

```rust
#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum AdvisorError {
    #[error("http transport: {0}")]   Http(#[from] reqwest::Error),
    #[error("subprocess io: {0}")]    Io(#[from] std::io::Error),
    #[error("json parse: {0}")]       Json(#[from] serde_json::Error),
    #[error("claude cli exited {code:?}: {stderr}")]
                                      CliFailed { code: Option<i32>, stderr: String },
    #[error("claude reported is_error=true: {0}")]
                                      ClaudeError(String),
    #[error("provider api {status}: {body}")]
                                      Api { status: u16, body: String },
    #[error("missing config key: {0}")] MissingKey(String),
}
```

**Module layout under `src/`:**

```
src/
  main.rs                 # exists — CLI, anyhow at top level
  recipe.rs               # exists — EditRecipe contract (authoritative)
  decode/
    mod.rs                # Decoder trait: preview(), exif()->Meta, render()->histogram
    rawler.rs             # primary impl (preview + EXIF + raw image)
    rawloader.rs          # fallback impl (imagepipe sRGB; LGPL pure-Rust)
  advisor/
    mod.rs                # Advisor trait, Preview, Meta, Verdict, AdvisorError
    openai.rs             # OpenAiProvider: reqwest, Responses API + json_schema (§3)
    claude.rs             # ClaudeProvider: tokio::process claude -p (§4)
  config.rs               # serde+toml load of autoshop.local.toml; dotenvy for .env
  xmp.rs                  # M2 — sidecar writer (§5), spec'd in M1
```

**Config / keys** [verified: dotenvy loads .env; toml via serde; claude CLI needs no key]:
- `dotenvy::dotenv()` at startup; `OPENAI_API_KEY` via `std::env::var`.
- `autoshop.local.toml` (gitignored, per [ARCHITECTURE.md:74](../docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)) holds non-secret knobs: model ids, base URLs, claude bin path, `extra_args=["--bare"]`.
- Add to `Cargo.toml`: `tokio` (rt-multi-thread, macros, process), `reqwest` (json, rustls-tls), `async-trait`, `dotenvy`, `toml`, `base64`, plus `rawler` (pinned) and optionally `rawloader`+`imagepipe`.

## 3. GPT vision request — concrete shape, model, structured output

**Chosen model: `gpt-5.5`** (best reasoning, vision + structured-output capable), with `gpt-5.4` / `gpt-5.4-mini` as cheaper config-swappable alternatives (2–7× cheaper) [verified: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models + pricing table]. All three are vision-capable and support Structured Outputs ("starting with GPT-4o") [verified: structured-outputs guide].

**Chosen API + method: Responses API with `text.format` json_schema, `strict: true`.** Preview passed as a base64 data-URL `input_image` with `detail:"high"` [verified: images-vision guide for `input_image`/`image_url`/`detail`; structured-outputs guide for `text.format`].

Concrete request body (schema is the **real `EditRecipe`** from `src/recipe.rs`, not Report 2's illustrative one). Every object sets `additionalProperties:false` and every property is in `required` [verified: those three rules are required for strict mode]:

```jsonc
{
  "model": "gpt-5.5",
  "input": [
    { "role": "user", "content": [
      { "type": "input_text",
        "text": "You are a photo-edit advisor. Given this RAW preview and its metadata/histogram, return an EditRecipe. Stay within documented ranges." },
      { "type": "input_image",
        "image_url": "data:image/jpeg;base64,{BASE64_PREVIEW}",
        "detail": "high" }
    ]}
  ],
  "text": { "format": {
    "type": "json_schema", "name": "edit_recipe", "strict": true,
    "schema": {
      "type": "object", "additionalProperties": false,
      "required": ["version","exposure_ev","contrast","highlights","shadows",
        "whites","blacks","temperature_k","tint","vibrance","saturation",
        "clarity","dehaze","sharpening","noise_reduction","straighten_deg",
        "crop","tone_curve","rationale","confidence"],
      "properties": {
        "version":{"type":"integer"},
        "exposure_ev":{"type":"number"}, "contrast":{"type":"number"},
        "highlights":{"type":"number"}, "shadows":{"type":"number"},
        "whites":{"type":"number"}, "blacks":{"type":"number"},
        "temperature_k":{"type":["number","null"]}, "tint":{"type":"number"},
        "vibrance":{"type":"number"}, "saturation":{"type":"number"},
        "clarity":{"type":"number"}, "dehaze":{"type":"number"},
        "sharpening":{"type":"number"}, "noise_reduction":{"type":"number"},
        "straighten_deg":{"type":"number"},
        "crop":{"type":["object","null"], "additionalProperties":false,
          "required":["left","top","right","bottom"],
          "properties":{"left":{"type":"number"},"top":{"type":"number"},
            "right":{"type":"number"},"bottom":{"type":"number"}}},
        "tone_curve":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object",
          "additionalProperties":false,"required":["input","output"],
          "properties":{"input":{"type":"integer"},"output":{"type":"integer"}}}},
        "rationale":{"type":"string"}, "confidence":{"type":"number"}
      }
    }
  }}
}
```

Note `temperature_k` and `crop` are `["number","null"]` / `["object","null"]` to match the `Option<…>` fields — strict mode requires every property present, so optionals are expressed as nullable, not omitted. After parsing, call `EditRecipe::clamp()` ([src/recipe.rs:135](../src/recipe.rs)) — never trust the model's ranges.

Image-input limits (well within our single small preview): ≤512 MB payload, ≤1500 images, PNG/JPEG/WEBP/GIF [verified: images-vision guide].

[unverified] exact numeric JSON-schema size/depth/enum limits — the "Supported schemas" subsection did not render in the fetched docs; our schema is small (≤24 properties, depth 3) so almost certainly fine, but confirm at the structured-outputs "Supported schemas" anchor if the schema grows.

## 4. Claude verifier — `claude -p` envelope parsing + `Verdict`

**Invocation (as planned, Report 3):** `claude -p --bare --model <model> --output-format json <prompt>`. `--bare` was believed mandatory — without it a project-level skill (`cc-enforcer`) + PROGRESS.md auto-load and pollute `.result` with a YAML block; `--bare` strips it and cut cost 16× ($0.111 → $0.0070) [verified: A1 runs].

> **Reversed in v0.11.2 — do not restore `--bare`.** Since claude CLI ≥ 2.1.210
> `--bare` also means "OAuth and keychain are never read", so under it the
> verifier could only authenticate from a stray `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and failed
> with an empty stderr. The shipped invocation is
> `claude -p --setting-sources "" --strict-mcp-config --disable-slash-commands
> --output-format json --model <model>`, which achieves the same clean envelope
> while keeping OAuth usable (`src/advisor/claude.rs`). Pass the prompt as the **final positional arg** (or via stdin) — variadic flags like `--add-dir`/`--allowedTools` swallow a trailing positional [verified: A2 failure]. The verify path is **data-only / no image**, so it needs no `--allowedTools`/`--add-dir` and runs permission-free [verified: A1].

**Envelope shape (verified raw stdout, single JSON object):**

```jsonc
{ "type":"result", "subtype":"success", "is_error":false,
  "result":"<the model's text reply>",        // <-- extract this
  "total_cost_usd":0.0070, "stop_reason":"end_turn",
  "usage":{...}, "modelUsage":{"claude-sonnet-4-6":{...}},
  "permission_denials":[], "session_id":"..." }
```

Parse plan (serde ignores unknown fields by default) [verified: serde.rs container-attrs]:

```rust
// src/advisor/claude.rs
let out = tokio::process::Command::new(&cfg.claude.bin)
    .args(["-p","--bare","--model",&cfg.claude.model,"--output-format","json", &prompt])
    .output().await?;                                   // -> AdvisorError::Io
if !out.status.success() {
    return Err(AdvisorError::CliFailed {
        code: out.status.code(),
        stderr: String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stderr).into_owned() });
}
#[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
struct Envelope { is_error: bool, result: String, subtype: String, total_cost_usd: f64 }
let env: Envelope = serde_json::from_slice(&out.stdout)?;   // -> AdvisorError::Json
if env.is_error { return Err(AdvisorError::ClaudeError(env.result)); }
// env.result is the model's verdict text; ask Claude to emit verdict JSON, then parse:
let verdict: Verdict = serde_json::from_str(&env.result)?;
```

To get a structured verdict, the prompt instructs Claude to reply with **exactly** a JSON object matching `Verdict`, then we parse `env.result` as that JSON (Claude has no `response_format`; we constrain by prompt + parse + retry-on-parse-fail).

**`Verdict` type** (matches [ARCHITECTURE.md:114](../docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) "accept / revise / reject + reasons"):

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Verdict {
    pub decision: Decision,
    pub reasons: Vec<String>,
    /// When decision == Revise, a short instruction for the next propose() round.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub revised_hint: Option<String>,
}
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum Decision { Accept, Revise, Reject }
```

A `Revise` (or `Reject`) verdict can trigger **one** revision round back through `propose()` with `revised_hint` injected ([ARCHITECTURE.md:114](../docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)).

Tooling note for the build harness [verified, not a Claude bug]: on this machine, drive Python via PowerShell, not the Bash tool (Git-Bash mis-passes args → `Non-UTF-8 code starting with '\x90'`).

## 5. XMP sidecar writer (M2 build, M1 spec-lock)

**Namespace:** `http://ns.adobe.com/camera-raw-settings/1.0/`, prefix `crs` [verified: developer.adobe.com/xmp/docs/XMPNamespaces/crs/]. **Sidecar naming:** `foo.ARW → foo.xmp` (replace extension, NOT `foo.ARW.xmp`) [verified: Adobe/Lightroom help corpus]. Scalars are **attributes** on `rdf:Description`; the tone curve is a **child `rdf:Seq` of `"x, y"` strings** [verified: real ACR sidecars]. `<?xpacket?>` wrapper optional [verified: KelSolaar gist].

**EditRecipe field → `crs:` key mapping** (field set from [src/recipe.rs](../src/recipe.rs); types/ranges from Reports 4 & 5):

| EditRecipe field | `crs:` key | Writable type | Conversion / caveat |
|---|---|---|---|
| `exposure_ev` | `Exposure2012` | real | identity — both stops/EV. Write decimal e.g. `"0.35"` [verified: XMP.pm; real sidecar `Exposure2012="0.00"`] |
| `contrast` | `Contrast2012` | integer | identity −100..100 [verified: XMP.pm integer] |
| `highlights` | `Highlights2012` | integer | identity [verified] |
| `shadows` | `Shadows2012` | integer | identity [verified] |
| `whites` | `Whites2012` | integer | identity [verified] |
| `blacks` | `Blacks2012` | integer | identity [verified] |
| `temperature_k` | `Temperature` | integer | Kelvin 2000..50000; valid as absolute only for RAW+Custom WB. `None` ⇒ omit key (as-shot) [verified: range Adobe/exiv2] |
| `tint` | `Tint` | integer | −150..150 in crs vs recipe's −100..100 — **scale/clamp on write** [verified: range Adobe/exiv2; recipe range src/recipe.rs:45] |
| `vibrance` | `Vibrance` | integer | identity −100..100 [verified] |
| `saturation` | `Saturation` | integer | identity −100..100 [verified] |
| `clarity` | `Clarity2012` | integer | identity −100..100 [verified] |
| `dehaze` | `Dehaze` | real | identity −100..100; absent in older sidecars — on read, score absent as neutral 0 [verified: XMP.pm real; exiftool forum] |
| `sharpening` | `Sharpness` | integer | identity 0..150 — **no rescale**; clamp only [verified v0.31.1: 15 real sidecars carry `crs:Sharpness="150"` (2 repos, NIKON Z 6 + Z 30, `crs:Version` 15.3 + 17.2), max of 566 observed occurrences. The earlier "crs 0..100, rescale ×⅔ on write" row was WRONG: it came from a third-party Lua slider table (`RobColeLr/…/DevelopSettings.lua` L165 min=0 max=100), not from Adobe, and the sidecars contradict it. 150 is the Detail > Sharpening Amount slider's UI maximum] |
| `noise_reduction` | `LuminanceSmoothing` | integer | 0..100; **easily-missed key** — must be written or NR is silently dropped [verified: standard crs, Report 5] |
| `straighten_deg` | `CropAngle` | real | degrees; recipe = clockwise-positive. **SIGN MEASURED 2026-08-19 (R27 P3): `straighten_deg = −CropAngle`** — Lightroom turns the CONTENT counter-clockwise by a positive `CropAngle`. The negation lives at the XMP boundary (`xmp::lr_to_engine_crop` / `engine_to_lr_crop`), and the value is written with six decimals, not one. |
| `crop.{left,top,right,bottom}` | `CropLeft/Top/Right/Bottom` | real | normalised [0,1], (0,0) top-left → identity; only applied when `HasCrop="True"` [verified: identity mapping; HasCrop gate] |
| `crop` present | `HasCrop` | boolean | `"True"` when `crop` is `Some`, else `"False"` [verified: real sidecar] |
| `tone_curve[{input,output}]` | `ToneCurvePV2012` | Seq of `"x, y"` | 0..255 ints; must start `"0, 0"`, end `"255, 255"`; ≥2 points; empty recipe curve ⇒ omit or write identity [verified: real sidecars] |
| (constant) | `ProcessVersion` | text | `"11.0"` for current PV5/2012 [verified key; "11.0" value [unverified]] |
| (constant) | `Version` | text | ACR plugin version string e.g. `"15.0"` [verified key/format] |

**Template** (`foo.xmp` next to `foo.ARW`; structure verified against real ACR sidecars):

```xml
<x:xmpmeta xmlns:x="adobe:ns:meta/" x:xmptk="Autoshop XMP">
 <rdf:RDF xmlns:rdf="http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#">
  <rdf:Description rdf:about=""
    xmlns:crs="http://ns.adobe.com/camera-raw-settings/1.0/"
    crs:Version="15.0"
    crs:ProcessVersion="11.0"
    crs:Temperature="{KELVIN_2000_50000 | omit if None}"
    crs:Tint="{-150_150}"
    crs:Exposure2012="{EV e.g. +0.35}"
    crs:Contrast2012="{-100_100}"
    crs:Highlights2012="{-100_100}"
    crs:Shadows2012="{-100_100}"
    crs:Whites2012="{-100_100}"
    crs:Blacks2012="{-100_100}"
    crs:Clarity2012="{-100_100}"
    crs:Dehaze="{-100_100}"
    crs:Vibrance="{-100_100}"
    crs:Saturation="{-100_100}"
    crs:Sharpness="{0_150}"
    crs:LuminanceSmoothing="{0_100}"
    crs:HasCrop="{True|False}"
    crs:CropTop="{0.0_1.0}"
    crs:CropLeft="{0.0_1.0}"
    crs:CropBottom="{0.0_1.0}"
    crs:CropRight="{0.0_1.0}"
    crs:CropAngle="{DEGREES}">
   <crs:ToneCurvePV2012>
    <rdf:Seq>
     <rdf:li>0, 0</rdf:li>
     <rdf:li>{X_0_255}, {Y_0_255}</rdf:li>
     <rdf:li>255, 255</rdf:li>
    </rdf:Seq>
   </crs:ToneCurvePV2012>
  </rdf:Description>
 </rdf:RDF>
</x:xmpmeta>
```

[unverified] the ±100 slider bounds, crop 0.0..1.0 fraction, `ProcessVersion="11.0"`, and ~~`CropAngle` sign~~ (**CLOSED 2026-08-19, R27 P3 — measured against rendered pixels on six photographs, not looked up: `rot(source → export) = −CropAngle`**) — these are well-established ACR convention but were not pin-confirmed in primary docs (Adobe helpx pages timed out). ## 6. Eval / style harness approach (M4, designed in M1)

Ground truth = the user's **finished edits**. Two cases ([ARCHITECTURE.md:129-134](../docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)):

**Case A — XMP/develop settings exist (primary scorer; recipe-vs-recipe in slider space).** Read the user's `crs:` keys with one `exiftool -j -struct -G1 …` call (`-struct -j` required because `ToneCurvePV2012` is a sequence). Per image compute signed delta `Δf = recipe_f − gt_f`; aggregate **per-field MAE** (which knob the AI gets wrong) and **signed mean bias** (the tuning signal). Tone curve: sample both as a 256-entry LUT and RMSE. Crop: IoU + angle delta. **Needs only exiftool + arithmetic** — the smallest, most certain toolchain, so it is the primary scorer. Mapping caveats carried from §5: `noise_reduction`→`LuminanceSmoothing` (must add to the exiftool key list or NR goes unscored), `Dehaze` absent ⇒ score as neutral 0 not unknown, `temperature_k` vs `Temperature` is an absolute-Kelvin compare **only** for RAW+Custom WB (else use `IncrementalTemperature` as relative), `straighten_deg` sign vs `CropAngle` must be verified on one known image [verified: exiv2 crs schema; exiftool Dehaze forum].

**Case B — only an exported JPEG/TIFF (render-vs-export).** Render the AI recipe through the M2 engine, center-crop both to common aspect + downscale to 1024px long edge, then compute: **mean & 95th-pct ΔE2000** via `colour.delta_E(lab_a, lab_b, method='CIE 2000')` [verified: colour.readthedocs.io signature]; **SSIM** on luminance via `skimage.metrics.structural_similarity(..., data_range=…)` [verified: scikit-image API]; histogram correlation; estimated EV offset (least-squares gain in linear light → `log2(g)`); estimated WB offset (channel-mean ratio on near-neutral mask). Auxiliary: `exiftool` the export — many retain `crs:` tags → partial fall-back to Case A.

**Tuning signal:** convert corpus stats into **prompt deltas** (measured per-field bias lines injected into the advisor prompt, regenerated each run), a scalar objective `score = w1·MAE_A + w2·meanΔE00 + w3·(1−SSIM) + w4·(1−hist_corr)` (Case A weighted to dominate when XMP exists), and a holdout **regression gate** wired into the same accept/revise loop as §4. **Cold-start:** few-shot the advisor with 3–6 diverse (preview + the user's exiftool-read settings) exemplars before any score history exists.

[unverified] "ΔE00 < 2 = imperceptible" is convention, not a re-derived constant; ~~the EV/WB estimators and gray-world-on-neutrals heuristic are estimates, not measurements — labeled inline so they aren't treated as ground truth.~~ **The estimator half of that sentence is retired 2026-08-19 (R27 Batch-6): they are measured now — §8 #12 carries r, slope, bias and MAE for each against 147 of the photographer's own sidecars.** Note what the measurement had to work around: **Case B above was never built**, so there were no Case-B estimators to test; the probe measures the one shipped implementation behind each name. Two of the three survive with numbers and **gray-world-on-neutrals is refuted outright**, so the paragraph's caution was warranted for exactly one of the three — and that one is now a documented do-not-build rather than an open label.

**Dependency reality:** `exiftool` is **not on PATH**, and `rawpy`/`cv2`/`skimage`/`colour` are **not installed** [verified: `which exiftool` empty; `import` → ModuleNotFoundError]. Install before M4: `exiftool` on PATH, `pip install colour-science scikit-image numpy` (opencv optional). Case A (exiftool + arithmetic) has no Python-lib dependency → make it the default scorer.

   *Accept:* config loads model ids / claude bin / `extra_args`; missing `OPENAI_API_KEY` yields `AdvisorError::MissingKey`, not a panic.

   *Accept:* compiles; a no-op mock impl satisfies `Box<dyn Advisor>` and is callable across a spawned tokio task.

   *Accept:* against a hand-written recipe+meta prompt, real `claude -p --bare` returns exit 0, envelope parses, and a valid `Verdict` JSON deserializes; an out-of-range recipe yields `Decision::Revise`/`Reject`.

   *Accept:* `cargo run -- advise sample.ARW` decodes → proposes → verifies → prints an `EditRecipe` JSON + `Verdict`; a forced bad recipe triggers exactly one revision round.

   *Accept:* a `recipe_to_crs(&EditRecipe)` map and the template render compile; a unit test emits a well-formed XMP string for a sample recipe (validate by reading it back with `exiftool` once exiftool is installed).

Measured by SIFT/RANSAC registration against un-straightened references on **six photographs** spanning −3.27°…+1.73°, best pair agreeing to 0.0002°, rival hypothesis separated by 34× the residual on the weakest row; a seventh (`_DSC9558`, `PerspectiveUpright=2`) is excluded WITH CAUSE, not silently. The route was (a) — library forensics, exactly as planned here — and it also found that the crop RECTANGLE was being read in the wrong frame (rotated corners of the source frame, not an axis-aligned box), that the ordering guard `left < right` silently discarded legal `Left > Right` crops, and that the writer's `{:.1}` cost 4.3 px of edge-to-edge tilt per re-save. | 12 | EV-offset, WB-offset, gray-world-on-neutrals estimators (heuristics) | **CLOSED 2026-08-19 (R27 Batch-6), by measurement over the 147-pair set — and one of the three is REFUTED.** First finding: the **Case B scorer these estimators were designed for was never built** (no `delta_E`/`ssim`/Case-B path exists in `src/`), so the row could not be closed by testing "the Case B estimators"; what it closes is the one shipped implementation per line. **EV-offset** = `advisor::HeuristicProposer::ev_offset_estimate` (`log2(118/mean_luma)`) against the photographer's `crs:Exposure2012`: **r = +0.637, slope 0.761, bias +0.179 stops, MAE 0.466, n = 147** — a content-blind histogram heuristic really does predict this photographer's exposure taste, which is the evidence `heuristic.rs`'s "not a placeholder stub" claim never had. **WB-offset** = `render::as_shot_wb` (McCamy CCT + Krystek Duv) against Adobe's OWN as-shot reading of the same file under `WhiteBalance="As Shot"` — two programs, one physical quantity, so this one is a MEASUREMENT, not taste: **Kelvin r = +0.955, MAE 183 K (≈3.2 %), bias −99 K, slope 0.898; tint r = +0.974, MAE 2.69, bias +2.26, slope 1.055; n = 84**. The `Duv × 3000` scale was calibrated on a single anchor ("D65 ⇒ ≈ +10"); 84 real files now say it is ~5 % hot with a +1.5 intercept — **registered, not acted on** (如实呈报不预改; it goes to the 目检包). **gray-world-on-neutrals** = `render::solve_wb_from_neutral` fed the frame's own mean RGB: **REFUTED — r = +0.058 over all 135 sidecars carrying a Temperature, and r = −0.002 on the 51-photo cohort where the photographer actually chose a WB.** It rails at the +40000 K ceiling on five frames and at −100 tint on five more, because a whole-frame mean of an already-white-balanced camera preview is a colour, not an illuminant. Scope of that verdict, stated precisely: the **solver** is not what failed (it is used in the product only by the WB eyedropper, on a patch the user asserts is neutral, which this probe does not test) — what is refuted is the gray-world **assumption** M1 proposed feeding it, so the practical consequence is a **do-not-build**. Probe: `eval`'s `#[ignore]`d `AUTOSHOP_ESTIMATOR_PROBE` (no API call, 45 s over the 147 pairs); raw output `~/.claude/plans/r27-materials/estimator-probe-147.txt`. |

Direct inspection of the user's library on 2026-06-26 resolves the pending inputs and
**supersedes several of the research guesses above with real values.** Evidence is the
user's own files; no `exiftool` was needed (a sidecar was read directly).

### 9.1 Dataset shape [verified: PowerShell census this session]
- Layout: `<library>\Raw\<year 2022–2026>\<shoot>\*.ARW` (+ `成片\` finished JPEGs, `相册\` album JPEGs, `To-Be-Sync'd\`).
- **3655 `.ARW`** originals (~400 GB). **153** of them have a matching basename `.xmp` sidecar → **eval Case A** (recipe-vs-recipe).
- **成片\ = 190 finished `.jpg`**; **87 exact-basename-match an `.ARW`** → **eval Case B** (render-vs-export). The rest are renamed/variant edits (`_DSC2065~4-edit`, `DSC01634_1`, `(1)`) or non-ARW phone/WeChat shots (`mmexport…`, `Weixin Image…`) — exclude the phone shots from the RAW-developer eval; recover renamed A7R edits via EXIF `DateTimeOriginal`+model matching, not filename alone.
- **The user confirmed both paths are wanted:** XMP when present, else analyse from the 成片 JPEG. Both are already in the eval design (§6).

### 9.2 Camera — single family → one decode target [verified: tiff:Model in 156 sidecars]
- **Sony A7R IV / A7R IVA only** — `ILCE-7RM4A` (146) + `ILCE-7RM4` (10). 61 MP, same sensor/ARW concerns.
- Both are 2019/2021 bodies → **outside `rawloader`'s frozen DB → `rawler` is confirmed required** (§1 decision validated against real bodies, not a guess).
- [unverified] actual `rawler` 0.7.2 decode of an `ILCE-7RM4A` `.ARW` — still the M1 task-1/2 acceptance check; not yet run.

### 9.3 Real `crs:` values — corrects §5/§8 guesses [verified: `<library>\Raw\2023\23-06-Cornwall-Raw\DSC08724.xmp`]
Use these, **not** the guessed constants in §5's template / §8's table:
- `crs:ProcessVersion="15.4"` (NOT `"11.0"` — closes §8 #10), `crs:Version="15.5.1"`, `crs:CompatibleVersion="234881024"`.
- Sliders are **signed integers with an explicit `+`**: `Contrast2012="+22"`, `Highlights2012="+7"`, `Shadows2012="-6"`, `Tint="+13"`, `Dehaze="+18"`, `Vibrance="+5"`, `Saturation="+13"`. `Exposure2012="0.00"` is decimal EV. `Sharpness="40"` plain unsigned int; `LuminanceSmoothing="0"` present. → §5's signed-int convention is right and the writer must emit the leading `+` for positives. *(v0.31.1: the "0..100" this bullet used to assert about `Sharpness` was an inference from one sample sitting at 40, not a measurement of the band. The band is 0..150 — see the §8 table row.)*
- `Temperature="5650"` is written **even when `WhiteBalance="As Shot"`** → refines §8 #14: `Temperature` is emitted as an absolute Kelvin regardless of WB mode in this corpus.
- Crop: `HasCrop="False"`, `CropTop/Left="0"`, `CropBottom/Right="1"`, `CropAngle="0"` → confirms 0..1 fractions + `HasCrop` gate (closes §8 #8). ~~`CropAngle` sign still [unverified] (no tilted sample in this file)~~ **— closed elsewhere: R27 P3 found seven tilted specimens in the user's own library (§8 #9).**
- **Tone curve correction:** real `ToneCurvePV2012` = `"0, 0"`,`"67, 61"`,`"189, 210"`,`"224, 255"` — the **last point need NOT be `"255, 255"`** (§5's template wrongly mandates it). Endpoints can be interior; only "starts at x=0, monotonic in x" holds.

### 9.4 Scope reality — user's edits exceed our global-only `EditRecipe` [verified: same file]
The real sidecar also carries keys we do **not** model: `Texture`, per-channel `ToneCurvePV2012Red/Green/Blue`, an Adobe `Look`/camera profile, lens-correction profile, and — most significantly — **`MaskGroupBasedCorrections`** (3 graduated-filter **local masks** with their own `LocalExposure2012`/`LocalTexture`/etc.).
- **Implication for eval Case A:** compare **only the global `crs:` keys** that map to `EditRecipe`; treat local masks / per-channel curves / profile as **out-of-scope for M1**, not as "AI error". Scoring unmodelled keys as misses would punish the AI for things it was never asked to produce.
- **Roadmap:** a future `EditRecipe` v2 could add a `masks: Vec<LocalAdjustment>` to chase the user's actual style; flagged, not silently dropped.

*v0.31.0 (R25) closure of this section.* Every item this paragraph listed as unmodelled now has a home, so the paragraph stands as history, not as current scope: `masks` landed in v0.22.0 (and R25 finally made LIGHTROOM's own masks importable — see ARCHITECTURE §4.5 「Import」); per-channel `ToneCurvePV2012Red/Green/Blue` are modelled globally and, since R25, **per mask** as LR's bare `MainCurve`/`RedCurve`/`GreenCurve`/`BlueCurve` (note the wire format differs from the global curve: no `PV2012` suffix, and **no space after the comma** — `<rdf:li>239,255</rdf:li>` vs the global `"67, 61"` of §9.3, so the two must never share a formatter); global `Texture` renders as of R25; the camera profile and Calibration/Transform blocks pass through **verbatim** (`Tier::PassThrough`, 16 named keys); the lens-correction profile is `RenderedNotExported` and discloses itself on save. What is still unmodelled is `crs:Look` (a nested element, not a flat property) and `PointColor` — and the merge preserves and NAMES them rather than dropping them.
- **Eval consequence, and why it is deliberately left to a re-baseline.** The exclusion above — "`Texture` is out-of-scope, not AI error" — was correct in M1 and is now wrong for `Texture`, which the engine renders. The eval ruler is derived from the control registry (R23-1), so a key changing tier changes the score; scores are ALREADY not comparable across R23 (the prompts were rewritten wholesale). ~~The R25 full re-baseline over the 147-pair set therefore IS the new reference~~ **— and by 2026-08-19 the R25 baseline had itself gone stale on three further axes (v0.31.1's `Sharpness` 1:1 correction, v0.32.0's (32, 20) px render shift, and R27's mask-import work). R27 Batch-6 attempted the HEAD re-run twice and both attempts died mid-run (photo 83/147: the machine hit a commit-memory wall; the chunked retry was cut short by a reboot the user ordered), so the re-baseline is MANDATED but NOT yet landed — the user ruled 2026-08-19 that it re-runs via the relay endpoint with the parallel `--jobs` work, inside R27. Until that file exists, R25's numbers remain the only citable reference** — and re-deriving old numbers against a new run would be arithmetic on two different rulers.
